data.title: Mycetoma (Madura foot) — viva
data.summary: Fungal infections · 11 viva questions with answers
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Mycetoma (Madura foot)** (Fungal infections)_

**Q1. Define mycetoma.**
- Chronic, localised, granulomatous infection of skin, subcutis and bone caused by fungi (eumycetoma) or aerobic actinomycetes (actinomycetoma), characterised by the triad of tumefaction, multiple draining sinuses and discharge of grains

**Q2. Who described it and what is the mycetoma belt?**
- Gill described it in Madura (Madurai) in 1842 (hence Madura foot); Carter named it mycetoma
- Mycetoma belt: between latitudes 15°S and 30°N — Sudan, Mexico, India, Venezuela, Senegal

**Q3. Common agents in India?**
- Actinomycetoma (commoner in India): Nocardia brasiliensis, Actinomadura madurae, A. pelletieri, Streptomyces somaliensis
- Eumycetoma: Madurella mycetomatis (black grains), Pseudallescheria boydii/Scedosporium (white grains)

**Q4. Grain colour and causative organism?**
- Black: Madurella (eumycetoma)
- White/yellow: Nocardia, Actinomadura madurae, Scedosporium
- Red: Actinomadura pelletieri
- Yellow-brown: Streptomyces somaliensis

**Q5. Differences between actinomycetoma and eumycetoma?**
- Actinomycetoma: faster progression, more inflammatory, earlier bone involvement (many small lytic lesions), grains small (filaments <1 µm), responds to antibiotics
- Eumycetoma: slow, well-defined, fewer large cavities, grains with hyphae 2–5 µm, needs antifungals ± surgery

**Q6. Why is mycetoma painless and why does it become painful?**
- Painless due to slow progression and possible anaesthetic effect of nerve involvement; pain appears with secondary bacterial infection or bone invasion

**Q7. Investigations?**
- Grain examination (KOH, Gram — actinomycetes Gram-positive), culture (Sabouraud's for fungi; LJ/blood agar for actinomycetes)
- Deep biopsy (wedge, not punch) — grains with Splendore–Hoeppli phenomenon
- X-ray (periosteal reaction, cavities, 'sunray'), USG (bright hyperreflective echoes from grains), MRI 'dot-in-circle sign' (grains in granuloma), FNAC, PCR/sequencing

**Q8. Treatment of actinomycetoma?**
- Welsh regimen: amikacin 15 mg/kg/day in cycles (3 weeks) with co-trimoxazole; modified Welsh with rifampicin
- Damle's regimen (India): intensive phase penicillin + gentamicin + co-trimoxazole, then maintenance doxycycline + co-trimoxazole
- Two-step: co-trimoxazole + dapsone (± rifampicin, doxycycline) for months

**Q9. Treatment of eumycetoma?**
- Itraconazole 400 mg/day (or voriconazole/posaconazole) for 9–12 months to shrink the lesion, followed by surgical excision with wide margins, then continue antifungal; ketoconazole no longer used (hepatotoxicity)

**Q10. Why is surgery under local anaesthesia avoided?**
- Infiltration may spread grains along tissue planes and cause recurrence; regional/general anaesthesia and bloodless field with tourniquet preferred

**Q11. Indications of amputation?**
- Advanced bony involvement with non-response to medical therapy, secondary infection threatening life

## Quick spotter facts
- Swollen foot with multiple sinuses discharging grains — mycetoma

_Sources: DYP Survival Guide for PG Dermatology Exam (Mycetoma); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e ch.19 (Deep fungal infections). Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
